title: A first-order flexible ELA model based on geomorphic constraints
author: Keeler, Rupper, et al.

steps.title: Download MATLAB ELA code
steps.instruction: Obtain the ELA model MATLAB repository (https://github.com/durbank/ELA-model) and use version v0.1.0 as referenced in the manuscript.

steps.title: Collect glacier geometry data
steps.instruction: Measure discrete bed‑topography points and glacier‑width points along the glacier centreline, including both the toe and the head; about ten quasi‑equally spaced points are usually sufficient, though more may be needed for complex beds.

steps.title: Create CSV files of measurements
steps.instruction: Save the centreline distance (meters) and corresponding bed elevations (m a.s.l.) in one CSV, and the centreline distance with glacier widths (m) in a second CSV.

steps.title: Format inputs for MATLAB
steps.instruction: Run the provided format_inputs.m script to convert the two CSV files into a MATLAB structure with four fields: X_dist[N×1], Bed_pts[n×2], Ice_surf[n×2], and Width_pts[m×2] as described in Table 1.

steps.title: Add tributary glacier data (optional)
steps.instruction: If tributary glaciers exist, prepare additional structures matching Table 1 and pass them to the ELA model after the Monte‑Carlo simulation count argument.

steps.title: Set Monte‑Carlo parameters
steps.instruction: Specify the number of Monte‑Carlo simulations to run; optionally edit the default error‑assumption values (zSTD = 25 m, wSTD = 60 m, tau_STD = 5.0×10⁴ Pa, rho = 917 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²) in the code before execution.

steps.title: Run ELA calculation
steps.instruction: Call the function ELA_calc.m with the formatted input structure, the chosen number of simulations, and any tributary structures; the function returns the estimated ELA and Monte‑Carlo uncertainty bounds.

steps.title: Generate centreline in ArcGIS
steps.instruction: In ArcMap, draw or compute a characteristic glacier centreline; this line will be used for all subsequent extractions.

steps.title: Extract bed elevation from DEM
steps.instruction: Along the centreline, sample the DEM to obtain bed elevation versus distance; export these values to a temporary.xls file.

steps.title: Estimate ice surface elevation
steps.instruction: Import the temporary.xls into MATLAB and run ice_thick.m (included with the ELA model) to compute ice‑surface elevations at the same centreline points.

steps.title: Import ice surface back to ArcMap
steps.instruction: Load the ice‑surface results into ArcMap and combine them with the centreline dataset.

steps.title: Define glacier outline
steps.instruction: Digitise the glacier boundary from aerial imagery (modern glacier) or from moraine positions (paleoglacier); this outline delineates the accumulation region.

steps.title: Compute orthogonal width lines
steps.instruction: At each discrete centreline point, draw a polyline orthogonal to the centreline at the ice‑surface elevation; intersect this line with the glacier outline (or with bed topography for paleoglacier accumulation zones) to obtain the glacier width at that point.

steps.title: Export final input CSV
steps.instruction: Save the three columns—distance down‑valley, estimated bed elevation, and estimated glacier width—as a .csv file ready for import to the ELA model.
